gaps.sentence: ___ poverty remains a serious problem in many large cities.
gaps.explanation: Uncountable abstract nouns in a general sense take no article.

gaps.sentence: ___ number of applicants has doubled this year.
gaps.explanation: 'The number of' takes a singular verb ('has'); 'a number of' would take 'have'.

gaps.sentence: He demands ___ answer before the end of the day.
___ noise pollution in cities is getting worse.
gaps.explanation: 'Noise pollution' as a general concept takes no article.

gaps.sentence: ___ few days he had left were spent packing.
___ unemployment has fallen sharply this year.
gaps.explanation: Unemployment as a general concept takes no article.

gaps.sentence: She's studying history at ___ University of Vienna.
gaps.explanation: University names with of-phrases take the: the University of Vienna.

gaps.sentence: She earns fifty pounds ___ hour as a consultant.
gaps.explanation: 'An hour' — the 'h' is silent, so it starts with a vowel sound.
